allocation: 10 per kind, uniform without replacement within sorted-ID strata, then seeded shuffle; unweighted by hits

items.title: ䷣ 明夷 (Míng Yí) - Darkening of the Light
items.conclusion: When light is obscured, protect clarity by withdrawing its display.
items.if: Clear signals are punished or extinguished.
items.then: Hide the light to preserve it, and wait for a safer time to re-emerge.

items.title: Mandatory PSR (G3)
items.conclusion: If you want execution to be pattern-governed rather than post-hoc rationalized, require a Pattern Selection Record (PSR) before execution, or a typed gap declaration.
items.if: you want work to be guided by shared patterns and constraints
items.then: require PSR (pattern selected) or Gap PSR (pattern missing) at G3 before G2 can run

items.title: Dead Code Hygiene
items.conclusion: Keep MUSN behaviour legible by pruning experiments, deprecated flows, and orphaned namespaces before they are mistaken for supported features.
items.if: Repository-transition diagnostics already insist on tracking code paths to explicit obligations.
items.then: Schedule periodic dead-code sweeps: identify unreferenced namespaces, obsolete protocol handlers, and one-off experiments; delete or archive them; and ensure devmaps point only at active code paths.

items.title: Problem node: unqueryable trails block recovery
items.conclusion: This is a problem-stating node: without a trail an agent cannot distinguish unexplored paths from rejected ones, so it repeats mistakes or cannot recover.
items.if: An agent may revisit prior states, learn from dead ends, or undo an action.
items.then: Treat this node as the landing point for @why edges from patterns that answer the unqueryable-trail recovery problem; solving it remains the mechanism pattern's work.

items.title: Problem node: fundamentals drowned by the letter-number backlog
items.conclusion: This is a problem-stating node: a fundamental gap (the missing Q(o|pi) constructor) sat always-renderable in the audit and never blocking, because the letter-number backlog and keyword-statuses drowned it out.
items.if: A queue of individually-validated tasks competes with a fundamental gap that blocks them all.
items.then: Treat this node as the landing point for @why edges from patterns that answer fundamentals-drowning; solving it is the :F class's job, not this node's.

items.title: Realtime Loop Success Signals
items.conclusion: Treat the loop as healthy when batches stay small, latency stays low, and JSONL output is continuous.
items.if: Batch latency stays under target, dropped_lines stay near zero, and JSONL records are continuous.
items.then: Keep current settings; focus on integration coverage and matcher quality, not tuning.

items.title: Next Steps to Done
items.conclusion: insist that each devmap clause tracks a `next[...]` entry—either a procedural move (tests to run, docs to update, evidence to gather) or an explicit `next[none-known evidence[...]]` when the prototype is verified and waiting for downstream uptake; when no next step is recorded, flag the clause `drift` until the owner adds blockers or declares the work finished
items.if: every devmap clause is supposed to tell the reader what to do next so prototypes keep moving toward “done”
items.then: insist that each devmap clause tracks a `next[...]` entry—either a procedural move (tests to run, docs to update, evidence to gather) or an explicit `next[none-known evidence[...]]` when the prototype is verified and waiting for downstream uptake; when no next step is recorded, flag the clause `drift` until the owner adds blockers or declares the work finished

items.title: An Ablation Axis Must Not Also Switch Off the Measurement
items.conclusion: When the mechanism under study is also the mechanism the instrument depends on, an ablation of that mechanism does not produce a dose-response curve — it produces a curve of how much instrument remains. Check that the ablation axis and the measurement window are disjoint before reading anything off the curve.
items.if: A learning-curve, dose-response, or truncated-budget design ablates the same process that the outcome measure reads.
items.then: Separate the two intervals explicitly. Vary the adaptation budget over a training interval that ends before the measurement window opens, and hold the mechanism identical across arms inside the measurement window; or adopt a readout that does not require the ablated mechanism to be live. Register the intervals, not only the budget levels, and state the predicted value of the zero-budget arm in advance.

items.title: Route Exploration and Pivot
items.conclusion: When a proof admits multiple candidate approaches, explore them as lightweight wiring diagrams with explicit status (solid/open/blocked) before investing deeply. Abandon blocked routes promptly, record why they fail, and pivot to the most structurally favorable surviving route.
items.then: 1. Sketch each candidate approach as a lightweight proof architecture: list the intermediate steps, mark each as solid (proved), open (plausible but unproved), or blocked (known obstruction). 2. Triage immediately: kill any approach with a blocked node unless the blockage can be circumvented cheaply. Deprioritize approaches with multiple sequential open nodes (each is a conjunctive risk). 3. Among surviving approaches, prefer the one with the fewest open nodes and the most independent sub-goals (parallel risk, not serial). 4. Record the abandoned approaches and their specific failure points. These are not wasted work — they constrain the search space and may inform future attempts. 5. When investing in the chosen approach, set a checkpoint: if a specific open node proves harder than expected, re-evaluate the triage rather than sinking further. + QUALITY-CRITERIA: Well-applied: - Each candidate approach is sketched with explicit node status, not just named ("try surgery" is insufficient; "Wall surgery: need normal map [open], need obstruction vanishing [open], need L-theory parity [unfavorable]" is correct). - Abandoned approaches have specific, documented failure points. - The pivot rationale is structural, not just "this one looks easier." - A checkpoint is set for re-evaluating the chosen approach. Badly-applied: - Premature abandonment: killing an approach because one step is hard, when the step is actually routine. Verify blockages before triaging. - Sunk-cost pursuit: refusing to abandon an approach after investing effort, despite blocked nodes. - Phantom triage: listing approaches without assessing node status, then "choosing" based on familiarity rather than structure. - Failure to record: abandoning an approach without documenting why, losing the constraint information for future work. + WHEN: A proof step has two or more candidate approaches, and at least one approach has non-trivial obstacles (unverified hypotheses, unfavorable parameter regimes, missing intermediate results). The obligation is significant enough that choosing the wrong approach wastes substantial effort.

items.title: Problem node: Snatch institutions need a theory of play, not only defence
items.conclusion: This is a problem-stating node at section grain for the snatch section: the README itself assessed the collection as "Not yet a complete theory of play" with six named gaps, and then recorded the gaps being filled -- the section's patterns exist to answer that assessed problem and the syllogism test (Alexander patterns ~= Ostrom institutions ~= policies) the section was commissioned for.
items.if: A library section is read as institutions-for-play and consulted by a served cascade (snatch-cascade consults 12 of its members).
items.then: This node is the landing point for the shared @why edges from the snatch patterns (mechanical pass, row L18 v2): the design-grain six are mapped to treatments G1-G5 in the README's Six patterns table, and the gap-filled play patterns are named in the gaps-filled record; per-pattern questions route to that record, not to invention here.

items.title: Calibrate Impact Promises to Current Indicator Capacity (Sketch)
items.conclusion: A service should only promise demonstration where the measurement base exists to support the claim. Where indicator capacity is partial, the promise must narrow with it.
items.if: The pattern operates on the axis: broad impact promise ↔ currently demonstrable impact promise.
items.then: State which practices are currently demonstrable, which are still development work, and align service claims with that distinction.

items.title: Futon1 Storage Coherence Guard
items.conclusion: keep Futon1 storage coherent by enforcing Charon-guarded invariant checks on every write, requiring a penholder registry entry for each model descriptor, and bootstrapping the penholder registry before first write to a new data dir
items.if: `app.store/tx!` runs a verify function on a preview conn and rejects writes when invariants fail, and `app.store-manager` installs the Charon guardian when `MODEL_VERIFY_ON_WRITE` is enabled
items.then: always enable `MODEL_VERIFY_ON_WRITE` in production, set `MODEL_PENHOLDER`, and run `scripts.charon-penholder-bootstrap` (or equivalent) once per new data root before starting the API; keep `BASIC_CHAT_DATA_DIR` isolated per running JVM + IMPLEMENTATION: `apps/graph-memory/src/app/store.clj`: `tx!` forbids `:skip-verify?`, verifies against a preview conn, and throws on invariant failure `apps/graph-memory/src/app/store_manager.clj`: installs `charon-guard/guard-event`, ensures descriptors, and checks invariants at startup `apps/graph-memory/src/app/invariants.clj`: `verify-event` enforces penholder registry membership for model descriptors `apps/graph-memory/src/scripts/charon_penholder_bootstrap.clj`: seeds the penholder registry with model descriptor entries + SETTINGS: BASIC_CHAT_DATA_DIR: data root (unique per JVM) MODEL_PENHOLDER: identity used for penholder certificates (e.g. user) MODEL_VERIFY_ON_WRITE: enable Charon guard on every write (default true) XTDB_CONFIG: path to XTDB config for canonical store

items.title: Term-to-Channel Traceability
items.conclusion: Require each score term to declare the observation channels and precision settings it consumed.
items.if: You want tuning decisions and failures to be diagnosable at the level of which evidence actually drove each score term.
items.then: Require every G term contribution to declare the observation keys it consumed, the precision channels applied, and the intermediate values used to compute that term, and persist this mapping alongside the score.

items.title: Exotype 248 (0xF8)
items.conclusion: Exotype 248 is encoded; program/params mapped from futon5; lift mapping not yet in registry.
items.if: You need an explicit, searchable exotype record.
items.then: Use the encoding fields for identification and the futon5 manifest for program/params until lift mappings land.

items.title: Verify the Logic Model Before Writing the Code
items.conclusion: When a mission's correctness is carried by INVARIANTS over a process (gates, admissibility, conservation rules), verify the DESIGN as a clojure.core.logic + pldb model over an abstract trace BEFORE writing the harness — a design is verified iff a witnessed conforming trace yields zero violations AND one adversarial trace per invariant is caught.
items.if: The mission's guarantees are expressible as relations over a process trace (a run = a vector of step/cycle records), and you want to know whether the invariants are mutually satisfiable AND each is enforceable — independently of, and prior to, the live harness.
items.then: Express the invariants as goal-queries (query-violations) over a pldb fact-database built from an ABSTRACT trace (snapshot → build-db → goals → query-violations, the house idiom of agency/logic.clj + portfolio/logic.clj). Verify with a self-validating fixture: (a) a witnessed CONFORMING trace must yield ZERO violations, and (b) for EACH invariant, a synthetic ADVERSARIAL trace violating exactly it must be CAUGHT. The model is offline-only for VERIFY; it may later register as live probe families during INSTANTIATE.

items.title: Name the Decision Before the Framework
items.conclusion: When a document exists to support an operational choice, it must name the choice before it unfolds the framework. The framework is there to warrant the decision, not to delay it. A reader who has to reconstruct the decision from pages of apparatus is being asked to do argumentative integration work the document should already have done.
items.if: The pattern operates on the axis: framework-display <-/-> decision-clarity. Irreducible: either the document names the choice early enough for the reader to evaluate the rest as warrant, or it makes the reader infer the choice from surrounding machinery.
items.then: Name the choice, then subordinate the framework to it. + COMPOSITIONS: (1) State the decision in one sentence: say what should be built, adopted, rejected, or handed off. Do this before the explanatory framework expands. (2) Recast early sections as warrants: after the decision is named, let each framework component answer a visible question about why that choice follows. (3) Title for claim, not furniture: section headings should tell the reader what argumentative work is being done, not merely how many parts are coming. (4) Audit by inversion: ask whether a reader could delete the framework section and still say what choice the paper supports. If not, the decision has been hidden inside its warrant. + CHECK: Engaged when the reader can identify the operational choice in the opening movement and can read the rest of the document as support for that choice. Failing when the framework is intelligible but its bearing on a specific decision is still implicit until late in the paper.

items.title: ䷅ 訟 (Sòng) - Conflict
items.conclusion: Conflict arises when forces oppose; clarity and restraint prevent escalation.
items.if: Goals or signals are misaligned and actions interfere.
items.then: Seek clarification and minimal resolution; avoid total confrontation.

items.title: Role × Value Diagnostics
items.conclusion: Current institutional reality distorts several of the Role × Value invariants. [👓/们 🌱/己]
items.then: Operate an explicit move on the named axis (see substructure below); steward the pattern against the declared discipline. The projection of institutional identity into actual behaviour reveals the productive tensions that Slide 3’s transformation pattern must address.

items.title: Plan Around the Nervous System, Not Against It
items.conclusion: Treat each person's depletion as legitimate data and plan the shared time around it — rest, alone-time, and early nights are moves that protect the relationship, not withdrawals from it.
items.if: one of you is depleted (illness, overwork, allergy season, the female horrors, a bad night) and the standing plan assumes full capacity.
items.then: name the capacity honestly, ask/offer for the lower-energy version (a quiet day, a night apart, a phone call instead of a visit), and hold it without penalty — 'that makes sense, I am tired too'.

items.title: Meet the Body Where It Hurts
items.conclusion: When the body flares — endometriosis, the cycle, exhaustion — name it plainly and meet it with attuned, non-fixing tenderness (a hot water bottle, company, rest), not problem-solving.
items.if: the body is in pain or depleted in a bodily way, and the reflex is either to hide it or to try to solve it.
items.then: name the flare plainly; respond with presence and small embodied comforts (hot water bottle, a quiet day, company); accept that the body sets the pace (see relationship-coherence/capacity-honoring).

items.title: Intent to Mission Binding (G5)
items.conclusion: If you want progress claims to be comparable across sessions, bind each task to an explicit mission reference and success criteria before authorization or execution.
items.if: you want the same "kind of work" to be evaluated consistently over time
items.then: require `:task/mission-ref` and `:task/success-criteria` and verify mission is active at G5

items.title: Fit-for-Use Stars
items.if: You want consistent, reusable objects.
items.then: Introduce multi-point “fit-for-use” ratings that capture practical readiness.

items.title: Invariants vs Repair
items.conclusion: if you want strict invariants but also operational resilience, pair enforcement with explicit repair and backfill pathways
items.if: you want invariants to halt corruption
items.then: enforce invariants strictly and maintain documented repair scripts for recovery

items.title: A New Failure Class Is A Design Defect, Not A New Species
items.conclusion: Treat every NEW failure class as a defect in the design that admitted it — eliminate it one layer down; the census of classes is closed, shrinking, and its growth rate is the reported metric.
items.if: A failure appears that fits no existing class.
items.then: Reverse the default. A new class opens a design question — what one layer down would make this shape impossible? — and the catch layer is the fallback only when that question has a recorded negative answer. Report the census and its growth rate wherever the apparatus reports health (the wm steward contract already requires growth rate alongside size — keep the two artifacts cross-cited).

items.title: IFR — FUTON2 Active Inference Energy (viriya)
items.conclusion: for every recorded episode, check that pivot streams, graph adapters, and presence bridges emit data usable by the FUTON3 proof engine and FUTON7 civic dashboards
items.if: FUTON2 exposes narratable AIF loops whose agents export state into FUTON1 and FUTON3
items.then: for every recorded episode, check that pivot streams, graph adapters, and presence bridges emit data usable by the FUTON3 proof engine and FUTON7 civic dashboards

items.title: Agent Contract
items.conclusion: Every agent operating in the FUTON stack must follow the agent contract: clock in, observe before acting, attribute all changes, respect invariants, and clock out with a proof trail.
items.if: The applicability scope of the pattern (see substructure). + AGENT-TYPES: - Human agents: Follow contract via tools (CLI, IDE integration) - AI agents: Follow contract via prompts and guardrails - Automated agents: Follow contract via code structure + CONTRACT-REQUIREMENTS: 1. CLOCK-IN/CLOCK-OUT: - Every session explicitly starts and ends - Session ID assigned at clock-in - Duration and outcome recorded at clock-out 2. OBSERVE-BEFORE-ACT: - Read state before proposing changes - Log observations as evidence - Never apply changes without observation phase 3. ATTRIBUTE-ALL-CHANGES: - Every change linked to agent identity - No anonymous mutations - Changes reference the observation that motivated them 4. RESPECT-INVARIANTS: - Check invariants before commit - On violation: stop-the-line, do not force through - Report invariant failures, do not hide them 5. PRODUCE-PROOF: - Every committed change has evidence chain - Proof path is replayable - Failed attempts also logged (for learning)
items.then: Operate an explicit move on the named axis (see substructure below); steward the pattern against the declared discipline. + ENFORCEMENT: - Session middleware rejects unclocked changes - Commit hooks verify agent attribution - Invariant checks block non-compliant commits - Audit logs flag contract violations

items.title: Refusal: :prediction-error/v1 / :source-field-missing
items.conclusion: A recurring refusal at :prediction-error/v1 is unresolved design work, not a standing red. Someone must decide whether the caller or the producer is wrong.
items.if: :prediction-error/v1 is asked for a value it can only supply from an input that was not observed or was malformed.
items.then: EMPTY. No resolution has been written. This half of the pattern is the tension recorded before its resolution exists, which is what the ruling extension asked for; it is NOT a claim that a resolution is known.

items.title: State-Snapshot-Witness: Periodic Point-in-Time Projection as Queryable Evidence
items.conclusion: For each long-lived runtime state container worth observing over time, the system periodically records a point-in-time projection of its full state as an evidence entry of shape `:event :state-snapshot` (or namespace-discriminated subtype). The snapshot is queryable after the fact, lets time-travel reconstruction work, and gives the apparatus a per-cycle witness of "what was true at boot N" without bespoke logging per inspectable subsystem. IC-state-snapshot-witness: For each registered `state-snapshot-witness/<container>` sibling, the durable evidence store carries at least one `:event :state-snapshot` (or namespaced subtype) entry per JVM boot, containing the full projection of the container's state at boot time. Reconstructing past state never requires evidence-aggregation gymnastics; one query returns one snapshot.
items.if: A long-lived state container's history is operationally meaningful (you'd want to ask "what was X at time T?" and have a direct answer).
items.then: Build sibling invariants under the relevant family with namespace IDs of the form `state-snapshot-witness/<container>`. Each sibling specifies four components: 1. **Container** — what long-lived state is being snapshotted (e.g. structural-law-inventory.sexp parsed; family-check-fns registry; git refs for ~/code/futon* repos; HUD widget last-render). 2. **Projection-fn** — `(fn [container]) → snapshot-data`. Produces a flat, EDN-serialisable map. Drops noisy fields; keeps semantically-meaningful state. 3. **Cadence** — at minimum boot-time (reachable-from-boot discipline) and on-demand. Optionally periodic via the canary apparatus. 4. **Emit-fn** — `(emit-snapshot! evidence-store snapshot-data)` writes one evidence entry through the boundary, tagged `[:invariant-queue :state-snapshot <container-id>]` with `:event :state-snapshot` (or namespaced subtype `:event :inventory-snapshot` etc.) carrying the full projection in `:body`. Wire each sibling at boot via `bootstrap.clj` (reachable-from-boot discipline — snapshot creation belongs in the construction path). Operator-on-demand variants live as `(snapshot-X-now! evidence-store)`. + EXEMPLAR INSTANCES: | Sibling | Container | Projection-fn | |---|---|---| | `state-snapshot-witness/inventory` | structural-law-inventory.sexp parsed | flatten families + scope-stack invariants to `[{:family-id :status :siblings [{:invariant-id :status :implemented-in}]}]` | | `state-snapshot-witness/registry` | `@futon3c.logic.probe/family-check-fns` | `(keys @registry)` plus per-family deferred?-flag | | `state-snapshot-witness/repo-refs` | `~/code/futon*/.git/HEAD` + active-branch | `[{:repo :branch :HEAD-sha :ahead-of-origin}]` | | `state-snapshot-witness/hud-render` | last HUD widget render | `{:widget-id :rendered-at :counts :motion-flag}` | + RELATED-MOVES: - `shape-first-identify` — methodological move that produces this shape. - `reachable-from-boot` — companion shape: snapshot creation belongs in the construction path. The two compose: snapshots ARE the structural witness that boot-time-construction worked. - `family-canary` — adjacent: per-family-fire evidence is the delta; the snapshot is the cycle-boundary state. Together they reconstruct full history.

items.title: Play the Authored Order First
items.conclusion: Name the identity temperament — the empty edit — and report every other temperament's score as a difference from it.
items.if: You have a cascade with an authored precedence and are considering a temperament that re-wires it.
items.then: Record the identity temperament as the run's temperament when it is the one in force, exactly as a non-empty one would be recorded, and state every other temperament's result as a delta against it on the same scenarios.

items.title: Devmap Cross-Reference
items.conclusion: Create a traceable mapping between implementation patterns and devmap prototypes.
items.if: You want to track how implementation work advances the higher-level devmap.
items.then: Record optional :pattern-ref metadata for fulab patterns and surface it in HUD summaries; treat missing refs as gaps until validation is enforced.
